summary:
I've been working on a few things across the homelab and the portfolio site.

The biggest is **Talk to Virtual Me**, a bounded career assistant that went live on phillipsben.com. It answers questions about my work using only what's published on the site — context-stuffed at ~12k tokens, no vector database. The interesting engineering problem was making confidential detail structurally impossible to leak: a build-time redaction guard strips sensitive material before it ever reaches the model, so the model simply can't be prompted into revealing it. Passed a 16-turn adversarial battery (fabrication attempts, prompt injection, open-relay role-play) with zero leaks. The backend benchmarking led to a deliberate call: local GPU prefill on the Pascal-era P100 was running 10–48 seconds cold, so the hosted model won on latency, with the local stack kept as an opt-in fallback.

**Switchboard** is the piece that makes multi-model homelab feasible on a single 16 GB Tesla P100. It's a FastAPI arbitration layer that serializes GPU access across inference backends — KoboldCPP for roleplay, ComfyUI for image generation, and the 26B brain that now runs my Hermes agent. The tricky part was the priority model: interactive site requests get a short preemption timeout and fall back to the cloud; batch agent jobs block and wait, because contending with a render mid-task is the whole point of having a broker. ComfyUI's GPU-coordinator custom node acquires a lease from Switchboard at the start of each render, so the 26B gets evicted cleanly instead of OOM-killing.

For the portfolio site itself, I generated and wired hero images for every project page using a ComfyUI pipeline on the P100 — abstract editorial linework duotoned to the site's two-color palette. The hard part was prompt discipline: the SDXL checkpoint treats literal nouns as permission to render architecture or scale figures. After a batch of failures, dot-field and stipple prompts proved far more reliable than line-centric ones. The build includes a prebuild guard that fails the build if a featured project is missing its hero.

**BudgetTracker** is a personal finance app I got deployed and working end-to-end this past month, after it sat dormant on a local machine. The interesting debugging was in the transaction categorization: a 429-storm from the bank API had run ~20 overlapping syncs with no single-flight guard, which raced past a check-then-insert dedup and produced 27,000 rows for 8,200 real transactions. Fixed with idempotent upserts and a filtered unique index, then used a reviewable SQL ruleset to classify ~7 years of backlogged transactions into meaningful categories. Connecting real balance data required catching that depository accounts show `available`, not `ledger` — the two diverge significantly because of pending holds.

highlights.oneLiner: Bounded career assistant live on phillipsben.com — context-stuffed, build-time redaction guard, 16/16 adversarial pass
FastAPI GPU arbiter serializing P100 across KoboldCPP, ComfyUI, and the 26B brain with priority-aware preemption
Generated and wired hero images for all project pages via a ComfyUI SDXL pipeline duotoned to the site palette
Fixed 429-storm dedup (27k rows → 8.2k), categorized 7yr backlog via SQL ruleset, corrected depository balance logic
